title: Bind the in-app assistant dock's build thread to the current app (reverses ADR-0057 A1.b per maintainer ruling)
body:
## Source

objectui#10899 item 4 (epic objectstack-ai/cloud#2440). When the maker opens the in-app assistant inside app 「客户管理」, the dock's build header chip reads 「构建 · 新建应用」. The dock uses the app-less, product-only build scope and sends no `packageId`, so the agent has to infer which app to edit.

The PR objectstack-ai/objectui#10924 dev root-caused it and deferred it because it reverses ADR-0057 Amendment A1.b.

## Maintainer ruling (epic session, 2026-09-28, verbatim)

「绑定当前应用（推荐）」

As presented: inside an authorable app (package not `com.objectstack.*`), when the resolved agent is `build`, the dock binds its build thread to that app. That means `editPackageId` is the app's package and the scope is `app:PKG:build`.
- The chip, the empty state and the agent context name the app.
- The dock, `/ai/build?package=PKG` and the Studio copilot share one thread; Maximize goes to `/ai/build?package=PKG`.
- `ask` stays ambient.
- Existing ambient build threads stay reachable in the `/ai` sidebar.

## Delivery shape

1. **ADR amendment.** An amendment to `docs/adr/0057-console-ai-chat-one-conversation-docked.md` records the reversal of the A1.b "dock keeps the legacy product-only key" line, citing this ruling.
   - `docs/adr/**` is a governed surface, so it is its own **draft** PR that the maintainer merges.
   - Do not mix it into the code PR.
2. **Code PR.** Implements the binding.
   - Reuse `editPackageId` / `chatConversationScope`; add no new surface.
   - Tests pin the chip text inside an app, the scope key, thread sharing with `/ai/build?package=`, and `ask` staying ambient.

## Acceptance

1. Inside app X, the dock's build chip names X, and the build request carries X's package id.
2. Opening `/ai/build?package=X` shows the same thread.
3. Outside any authorable app, behaviour is unchanged.
